slots.practicalActivity: Sign up for an Azure Databricks workspace (trial or your own subscription), then walk the real UI tour: open the Data, Workflows, Compute, and Catalog tabs in the left sidebar and note what each one is for before you touch a cluster or notebook.
slots.deliverable: A working Azure Databricks workspace, with written notes identifying what each of the four main sidebar tabs (Data, Workflows, Compute, Catalog) is used for.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a real all-purpose cluster with autoscaling (min/max workers) and an auto-termination timeout set, then open the Job Cluster configuration screen and compare which settings are and aren't available there.
slots.deliverable: One running all-purpose cluster with autoscaling and auto-termination configured, plus written notes on two concrete differences between it and a job-cluster configuration.

lessons.title: Attaching a Notebook to a Cluster

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new notebook and write at least one Python cell, one %sql cell, and one %md cell in it, then attach it to your Lesson 4 cluster, run all cells, detach the notebook, and reattach to confirm the Python state reset.
slots.deliverable: A saved multi-language notebook with working Python, SQL, and Markdown cells, attached to a live cluster with all cells successfully executed.

slots.practicalActivity: Upload a real NYC Taxi trip CSV file to DBFS, read it into a DataFrame with spark.read.csv("/FileStore/..."), then add a text widget to the notebook that parameterizes the file path so changing the widget value loads a different file.
slots.deliverable: A notebook that reads an NYC Taxi CSV from DBFS through a widget-driven file path, proven by changing the widget and re-running the read.

lessons.title: Databricks CLI and REST API Basics

slots.practicalActivity: Check which Databricks Runtime version your cluster is running, schedule your Lesson 6 notebook as a Job that runs on a daily trigger, then install/configure the Databricks CLI and run `databricks jobs list` to see that same Job from the command line.
slots.deliverable: One scheduled Job definition visible both in the Workflows UI and in CLI output from `databricks jobs list`.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Databricks Fundamentals: starting from a blank workspace, create a cluster, build a notebook that reads the NYC Taxi CSV from DBFS using a widget-driven path, and schedule that notebook as a Job — combining compute, notebooks, DBFS, widgets, and Jobs into one working chain.
slots.deliverable: One end-to-end lab artifact: a cluster, a widget-parameterized notebook reading real NYC Taxi data from DBFS, and a Job that runs it on a schedule.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the same NYC Taxi trips DataFrame out twice — once as a plain Parquet folder and once as a Delta table — to two different DBFS paths, then browse both folders with %fs ls to see the _delta_log directory Delta adds.
slots.deliverable: Two folders written from the same trips DataFrame (Parquet and Delta) with a short written comparison of their file listings.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a managed Delta table named trips from the NYC Taxi data with CREATE TABLE trips USING DELTA AS SELECT ..., then read it back twice — once with a SQL SELECT and once with spark.read.table("trips") in a Python cell.
slots.deliverable: A queryable managed Delta table named trips, with a notebook showing both a SQL query and a DataFrame-API read against it returning matching row counts.

slots.practicalActivity: Run two or three INSERT/append operations against your trips table, then open the _delta_log folder directly, read one of the raw JSON commit files, and match its add/remove actions to the corresponding row in DESCRIBE HISTORY trips.
slots.deliverable: A notebook that opens one raw _delta_log JSON commit file and explains, in writing, which table operation it corresponds to.

slots.practicalActivity: Try to append a DataFrame with an extra column to trips and capture the schema-mismatch error Delta throws, then re-run the same append with .option("mergeSchema", "true") so it succeeds and the new column appears.
slots.deliverable: A notebook showing the failed append with its schema-enforcement error message, followed by a successful mergeSchema append that added the new column.

slots.practicalActivity: After a few more writes to trips, query an earlier version with both SELECT * FROM trips VERSION AS OF n and TIMESTAMP AS OF, then use RESTORE TABLE trips TO VERSION AS OF n to roll the table back and confirm the row count changed.
slots.deliverable: A notebook comparing row counts between the current version of trips and an earlier version pulled via VERSION AS OF, plus one successful RESTORE TABLE run.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a new_trips DataFrame containing a mix of corrected existing trip_ids and brand-new trip_ids, then write a MERGE INTO trips AS target USING new_trips AS source statement with WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE and WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT, and confirm both kinds of rows landed correctly.
slots.deliverable: A working MERGE INTO upsert script plus before/after row counts in trips showing both an update and an insert actually happened.

slots.practicalActivity: Check the number of underlying files for trips with DESCRIBE DETAIL, run OPTIMIZE trips to compact them, check the file count again, then run VACUUM trips RETAIN 168 HOURS and confirm it completes without deleting files still needed by recent time-travel versions.
slots.deliverable: Before/after file counts from DESCRIBE DETAIL showing OPTIMIZE reduced the file count, plus a completed VACUUM run with its retention setting documented.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Delta Lake: take the trips table through a full lifecycle in one sitting — enforce then evolve its schema, upsert new records with MERGE, time-travel back to an earlier version, then OPTIMIZE and VACUUM it — documenting the output of each step.
slots.deliverable: One lab notebook exercising every Delta Lake operation from this chapter (schema enforcement/evolution, MERGE, time travel, OPTIMIZE, VACUUM) against the same trips table.

slots.practicalActivity: In a markdown cell, sketch the bronze/silver/gold flow specifically for the NYC Taxi data, naming the actual table you'll build at each layer (bronze.trips, silver.trips, gold.daily_revenue) before writing any code.
slots.deliverable: A documented bronze -> silver -> gold design, naming the specific NYC Taxi table at each layer, saved as a markdown cell.

lessons.title: The Silver Layer — Cleaned and Conformed Data

slots.practicalActivity: Create bronze.trips (the raw NYC Taxi CSV loaded untouched, including malformed rows), silver.trips (same data with fare_amount cast to double and duplicates dropped), and gold.daily_revenue (silver.trips grouped by day with summed fare_amount) as three separate Delta tables.
slots.deliverable: Three populated Delta tables — bronze.trips, silver.trips, and gold.daily_revenue — each queryable and each with a visibly different row count or column shape from the last.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the actual transformation code for both steps: a bronze-to-silver cell that casts types and deduplicates bronze.trips into silver.trips, and a silver-to-gold cell that groups silver.trips by day into gold.daily_revenue — run both against your Lesson 16 tables.
slots.deliverable: Two working transformation cells (bronze-to-silver, silver-to-gold) that successfully rebuild silver.trips and gold.daily_revenue from scratch.

slots.practicalActivity: Rewrite your silver-to-gold aggregation so it only reprocesses rows for days affected by new silver.trips data, instead of recomputing all of gold.daily_revenue from scratch on every run.
slots.deliverable: An incremental version of the silver-to-gold aggregation that updates only the affected day(s) in gold.daily_revenue, verified by adding one new row and checking only its day's total changed.

slots.practicalActivity: Set up Autoloader with .format("cloudFiles") pointed at a DBFS folder of NYC Taxi CSVs, start the stream writing into bronze.trips, then drop a new CSV file into the source folder and confirm it's picked up and ingested within seconds.
slots.deliverable: A running Autoloader stream, with evidence (a query of bronze.trips before/after) that a newly-dropped CSV file was automatically ingested.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a basic readStream against bronze.trips and a writeStream to a console/memory sink, start it, and watch its micro-batch progress live in the notebook's streaming dashboard as new data arrives.
slots.deliverable: A running structured streaming query with at least two completed micro-batches visible in its progress dashboard.

slots.practicalActivity: Convert your Lesson 29 silver-cleaning logic into a foreachBatch streaming job that reads from bronze.trips and MERGEs each micro-batch into silver.trips, then start it and confirm silver.trips keeps growing as new files arrive.
slots.deliverable: A continuously running bronze-to-silver streaming job using foreachBatch + MERGE, with silver.trips's row count increasing across at least two micro-batches.

lessons.title: Data Quality Checks in the Medallion Flow

slots.practicalActivity: Add a 3-day lookback window to your streaming silver job so it reprocesses recent dates for late-arriving trips, and add a quarantine.trips table plus a quality-metrics table that capture any row failing a basic check (e.g. negative fare_amount) instead of silently dropping it.
slots.deliverable: A quarantine.trips table containing deliberately-bad rows that were rejected, plus a quality-metrics table tracking the rejection rate over at least two runs.

slots.practicalActivity: Assemble bronze_ingest (Autoloader), silver_clean (foreachBatch + MERGE, with late-data and quarantine logic), and gold_aggregate (incremental daily revenue) into one Databricks Job with three chained tasks and task dependencies, then trigger a full run.
slots.deliverable: One multi-task Databricks Job (bronze_ingest -> silver_clean -> gold_aggregate) that completes a full run successfully, visible in the Job run's task graph.

slots.practicalActivity: Hands-on lab: pick one specific trip_id and trace it end to end through your Chapter 3 pipeline — confirm it lands in bronze.trips, gets cast/deduplicated into silver.trips, and is reflected in that day's gold.daily_revenue total.
slots.deliverable: A notebook that looks up the same trip_id across bronze.trips, silver.trips, and gold.daily_revenue and documents its transformation at each stage.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the lab: deliberately drop a malformed CSV (bad types, negative fares, duplicate trip_ids) into the Autoloader source folder and verify your quarantine.trips table and quality-metrics table catch the bad rows without corrupting silver.trips or gold.daily_revenue.
slots.deliverable: Query output proving a deliberately-bad file was quarantined rather than corrupting silver.trips or gold.daily_revenue, captured as the chapter's final checkpoint.

slots.practicalActivity: Without creating anything yet, write out the catalog.schema.table name you'd give each of your existing Chapter 3 tables (bronze.trips, silver.trips, gold.daily_revenue, quarantine.trips) under Unity Catalog's three-level namespace.
slots.deliverable: A written mapping of all four Chapter 3 tables to real catalog.schema.table names you intend to create next lesson.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a real catalog and schema (e.g. nyc_taxi.medallion) using CREATE CATALOG / CREATE SCHEMA, migrate bronze.trips into it as a managed table, create silver.trips as an external table pointing at a cloud storage path, then DROP TABLE each one and check whether the underlying files survived.
slots.deliverable: One managed and one external table under your new catalog.schema namespace, with written notes on what DROP TABLE did to each one's underlying files.

slots.practicalActivity: GRANT SELECT ON nyc_taxi.medallion.gold_daily_revenue to a second group/principal in your workspace, REVOKE it, then create a row filter function that restricts which VendorID rows a given role can see on gold_daily_revenue.
slots.deliverable: A documented GRANT/REVOKE sequence plus a working row-level security filter applied to gold_daily_revenue.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Catalog Explorer's lineage graph for gold_daily_revenue and trace it visually back through silver_trips to bronze_trips, then create a Unity Catalog Volume and load your raw NYC Taxi CSVs into it instead of DBFS.
slots.deliverable: A documented lineage trace from gold_daily_revenue back to bronze_trips, plus a populated Unity Catalog Volume containing the raw source files.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Delta Share exposing gold_daily_revenue to an external recipient, then audit your own catalog.schema setup against this lesson's best-practices checklist (naming consistency, least-privilege grants, external-location usage).
slots.deliverable: A configured Delta Share for gold_daily_revenue plus a short written best-practices audit of your own catalog, noting at least one thing you'd fix.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Unity Catalog: bring your entire Chapter 3 medallion pipeline fully under governance — a real catalog.schema namespace, bronze/silver as managed tables and a gold table in an external location, grants restricting who can query bronze directly, and a verified end-to-end lineage trace.
slots.deliverable: The full bronze/silver/gold pipeline running entirely inside a governed Unity Catalog catalog, with at least one grant and one verified lineage trace as evidence.

slots.practicalActivity: Review the Lakeflow Connect ingestion sources available in your workspace and write a short comparison of how one would replace your Chapter 3 Autoloader-based ingestion of the NYC Taxi files.
slots.deliverable: A written comparison of Lakeflow Connect vs. your existing Autoloader approach for ingesting the NYC Taxi CSVs.

slots.practicalActivity: Rewrite bronze_trips as a @dlt.table function (readStream.format("cloudFiles") over the NYC Taxi CSVs, with a comment and table_properties), add a @dlt.view intermediate casting step, and run it as a Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline.
slots.deliverable: A running Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline with at least one @dlt.view and one @dlt.table producing a materialized bronze_trips table.

slots.practicalActivity: Add @dlt.expect / expect_or_drop constraints to your silver_trips table definition (e.g. fare_amount >= 0, trip_id IS NOT NULL), run the pipeline once in triggered mode and once in continuous mode, and compare the run behavior and expectation metrics.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline run showing expectation pass/fail counts for silver_trips, plus written notes on the triggered-vs-continuous difference you observed.

slots.practicalActivity: Orchestrate your Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline as a task inside a Lakeflow Job, trigger a run, then use the pipeline's graph view and event log to check per-table row counts and expectation metrics for bronze_trips, silver_trips, and gold_daily_revenue.
slots.deliverable: A successful orchestrated Job run plus a reviewed pipeline graph showing row-count and expectation metrics for all three tables.

lessons.title: Course Recap — From Storage to Orchestrated Pipelines

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short comparison of how your Lakeflow pipeline differs from an Azure Data Factory pipeline covering the same bronze/silver/gold flow, then re-open your Chapter 1-5 lab artifacts and confirm each one still runs against your current catalog.
slots.deliverable: A written Lakeflow-vs-ADF comparison plus a self-audit confirming every chapter's lab artifacts still execute successfully.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone lab: rebuild the entire medallion pipeline (bronze_trips, silver_trips, gold_daily_revenue) as a single Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline with expectations enforced, replacing the manual Autoloader/foreachBatch/Job version from Chapter 3.
slots.deliverable: One Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline that reproduces the full bronze/silver/gold medallion flow with data-quality expectations enforced end to end.

slots.practicalActivity: Course review session: re-run your Delta Lake, medallion pipeline, Unity Catalog governance, and Lakeflow lab notebooks end to end against the real NYC Taxi dataset, confirm the governed, Lakeflow-orchestrated pipeline still produces a correct gold_daily_revenue, and note any lesson you'd revisit before moving on to Microsoft Fabric & Real-Time Analytics.
slots.deliverable: A completed course checklist confirming every lab (Delta operations, medallion pipeline, Unity Catalog governance, Lakeflow pipeline) runs successfully end to end.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can design and run a real bronze/silver/gold Delta Lake pipeline in Azure Databricks -- from Autoloader ingestion and MERGE-based upserts through Unity Catalog governance to an orchestrated Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline with enforced data-quality expectations -- not just describe the architecture on a whiteboard.
